docs.text: PRIME: Peptide Representation & Property Prediction ¶ PRIME is a modular toolkit designed for robust peptide property prediction and uncertainty estimation powered by protein language models (ESM-2). Key Highlights ¶ ESM-Powered Embeddings : Leverages transformer representations to capture complex biochemical and evolutionary features from sequence data alone. Redundancy Reduction : Integrates CD-HIT and sequence homology validation via BLAST to ensure rigorous, non-contaminated train/test partitioning. Uncertainty & Robustness : Multi-seed bootstrap evaluations, Monte Carlo Dropout, and SMOTE class imbalance compensation. Ensemble Inference : Evaluates target peptides across 15 models per feature and computes consensus probability and variance metrics. Workflow at a Glance ¶ The PRIME pipeline consists of three core stages: graph LR A[Raw FASTA Dataset] -->|prime-process| B[Clean Train/Test Sets] B -->|prime-uncert| C[Trained Models & Uncertainty Metrics] D[Target Peptides FASTA] & C -->|prime-predict| E[Final Predictions CSV] prime-process : Removes redundant sequences and splits datasets cleanly. prime-uncert : Trains downstream neural network / logistic regression heads across multiple random seeds. prime-predict : Runs ensemble inference on novel peptide candidates. Next Steps ¶ Check out the Installation Guide to set up your environment. Follow the Quickstart Guide to run your first pipeline. Read the CLI Reference for full parameter documentation.

docs.text: Installation ¶ This guide walks you through setting up the environment and installing the PRIME package. Prerequisites ¶ Operating System : Linux (recommended for GPU acceleration) or macOS. Python : Version 3.10+ (tested with Python 3.13 / 3.14). Conda : Miniconda or Anaconda . GPU (Optional but Recommended) : NVIDIA GPU with CUDA support for accelerated ESM embedding inference. 1. Environment Setup ¶ Create the Conda environment using the repository's environment file: conda env create -f tl_env.yml conda activate tl_env 2. Package Installation ¶ Install the PRIME package in editable mode from the repository root: cd prime pip install -e . This installs the package and registers the three command-line tools in your PATH: - prime-process - prime-uncert - prime-predict 3. Verify Installation ¶ Check that the CLI tools are available and display their help menus: prime-process --help prime-uncert --help prime-predict --help

docs.text: Methodology & Architecture ¶ This document outlines the theoretical and architectural design behind PRIME. 1. Sequence Representation (ESM Embeddings) ¶ Traditional peptide feature engineering relies on hand-crafted physicochemical properties (such as charge, hydrophobicity, or amino acid composition). PRIME utilizes ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling) , a transformer-based masked language model trained on millions of evolutionary protein sequences: - Tokenization : Sequences are mapped into residue tokens with start/stop boundary tokens. - Hidden Representations : The last hidden layer captures high-level context, secondary structure tendencies, and evolutionary conservation. - Pooling : An attention-masked mean pooling operation collapses residue embeddings across sequence length into a fixed-size embedding vector (e.g. 320 dimensions). 2. Redundancy Control ¶ To prevent optimistic bias and test-set leakage, prime-process applies strict sequence homology partitioning: - CD-HIT : Eliminates near-identical duplicates above a specified identity threshold (e.g., 70%). - BLAST Identity Check : Verifies cross-partition coverage and alignment metrics to ensure test sequences test generalizability rather than memorization. 3. Epistemic Uncertainty Estimation ¶ Predictions in drug discovery and therapeutic peptide design require confidence estimates: - Multi-Seed Variance : Models trained with different random seeds capture variance introduced by initialization, cross-validation folds, and SMOTE resampling. - Monte Carlo Dropout : During inference or evaluation, dropout remains active across passes to evaluate parameter posterior uncertainty. - Bootstrap Validation : Non-parametric bootstrap resampling (e.g. 1,000 iterations) generates 95% confidence intervals for ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Accuracy, F1-score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient. 4. Multi-Model Ensemble ¶ During inference ( prime-predict ), each peptide is evaluated across $M$ models (typically $M=15$ seeds per property): $$\bar{P} i = \frac{1}{M} \sum {m=1}^{M} P_{i,m}$$ $$\sigma_i = \sqrt{\frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{m=1}^{M} (P_{i,m} - \bar{P}_i)^2}$$ Where: - $\bar{P}_i$ is the ensemble mean probability for sequence $i$. - $\sigma_i$ quantifies model epistemic disagreement (uncertainty).

docs.text: Quickstart Guide ¶ This tutorial guides you through the end-to-end PRIME workflow: preprocessing raw data, training multi-seed models, and predicting properties for new peptide sequences. Step 1: Preprocess Sequences ( prime-process ) ¶ Prepare raw sequences by clustering with CD-HIT (to reduce sequence redundancy) and partitioning into train and test sets: prime-process \ --file data/antimicrobial.merged.fasta \ --output results/nonr \ --name Antimicrobial This creates: - results/nonr/Antimicrobial-train.fasta - results/nonr/Antimicrobial-test.fasta - results/nonr/Antimicrobial_blast_hits.png Step 2: Train with Uncertainty ( prime-uncert ) ¶ Train the downstream classification head using ESM embeddings across multiple random seeds: prime-uncert \ --train results/nonr/Antimicrobial-train.fasta \ --test results/nonr/Antimicrobial-test.fasta \ --name Antimicrobial \ --base-model /data/tiago/prime-validation/checkpoint-500000 \ --seed 42 \ --smote \ --device cuda \ --model-dir results/saved_models \ --embedding-cache-dir results/embedding_cache \ --output-dir results/uncertainty Repeat this step for your chosen seeds (e.g., 42, 43, 44, 45, 46, ... ) to build an ensemble. Step 3: Run Inference ( prime-predict ) ¶ Predict properties for novel peptide sequences using the trained models: prime-predict \ --input peptides_to_test.fasta \ --model_dir results/saved_models \ --checkpoint /data/tiago/prime-validation/checkpoint-500000 \ --device cuda \ --output final_predictions.csv \ --include_pred \ --include_std The resulting final_predictions.csv contains the mean predicted probabilities, uncertainty standard deviations, and consensus binary predictions for every target feature.

docs.text: prime-predict ¶ The prime-predict CLI provides multi-model ensemble inference on target peptide sequences. It extracts ESM representations once in-memory and averages predictions across all available seed models for each property. Command Syntax ¶ prime-predict [OPTIONS] Options ¶ Option Shorthand Type Default Required Description --input -i Path — Yes Input FASTA file containing candidate peptide sequences. --model_dir --model-dir Path — Yes Directory containing the trained .pkl model artifacts. --output -o Path predictions.csv No Path to the destination CSV file for predictions. --device -d Choice cpu No Compute device: cpu , cuda , or gpu . --checkpoint -c Path /data/.../checkpoint-500000 No Path to the ESM base model checkpoint directory. --include_pred --include-pred Flag False No Include binary classification ( 0 or 1 ) based on mean threshold. --include_std --include-std Flag False No Include standard deviation (epistemic uncertainty) across seeds. Features Discovered Automatically ¶ When pointing --model_dir to a directory containing models named like: Antimicrobial_old_celio_merged_seed_42_model.pkl Toxicity_old_celio_merged_seed_42_model.pkl Hemolitic_old_celio_merged_seed_42_model.pkl The CLI automatically parses the prefix before the first underscore ( _ ), groups the models into feature ensembles (e.g. 15 models per feature), and runs predictions across all features in a single pass. Output CSV Structure ¶ Column Description sequence_id Identifier extracted from the FASTA header ( >id ). sequence Canonical amino acid sequence. <Feature>_prob_mean Ensemble mean probability for the positive class (e.g. 0.98540 ). <Feature>_prob_std (Optional, if --include_std ) Standard deviation across the 15 models. <Feature>_pred (Optional, if --include_pred ) Binary consensus decision ( 1 if prob $\ge$ threshold, else 0 ). Example ¶ prime-predict \ --input novel_candidates.fasta \ --model_dir /data/saved_models \ --checkpoint /data/checkpoint-500000 \ --device gpu \ --output final_results.csv \ --include_pred \ --include_std

docs.text: prime-process ¶ The prime-process CLI handles data quality control, sequence deduplication, dataset splitting, and homology verification between partitions. Command Syntax ¶ prime-process [OPTIONS] Options ¶ Option Shorthand Type Required Description --file -f Path Yes Path to the raw input FASTA file to clean. --output -o Path Yes Directory path where output files will be written. --name -n String Yes Dataset/task prefix name (e.g. Antimicrobial , Toxicity ). --help No Show help message and exit. Algorithm Details ¶ CD-HIT Clustering : Redundant sequences sharing sequence identity higher than the configured threshold (default 0.7 in Params.yaml ) are clustered, retaining only representative sequences. Stratified Splitting : Sequences and labels are partitioned into stratified training and testing sets (default test size: 10% ). BLAST Homology Verification : BLAST ( blastp-short ) is performed between the training and test sets to quantify cross-partition similarity and query coverage. BLAST Scatter Plot : Generates a high-resolution scatter plot ( <output>/<name>_blast_hits.png ) correlating sequence identity with query coverage, with marker sizes reflecting bit scores and colors reflecting E-values. Example ¶ prime-process \ --file /data/raw/toxicity.fasta \ --output results/nonr \ --name Toxicity

docs.text: prime-uncert ¶ The prime-uncert CLI performs embedding-based training of PyTorch classifiers, epistemic uncertainty estimation, bootstrap evaluations, and model serialization. Command Syntax ¶ prime-uncert [OPTIONS] Options ¶ Option Type Default Required Description --train Path — Yes Training FASTA file with sequence labels encoded in headers. --test Path — Yes Test FASTA file with sequence labels encoded in headers. --name String — Yes Project or target property name (e.g. Hemolitic ). --base-model Path — Yes Path to the pre-trained ESM base model or checkpoint directory. --seed Integer 42 No Random seed for data splitting and model initialization. --smote Flag False No Enables SMOTE oversampling on training embeddings. --device String cuda / cpu No Compute device for embedding extraction and training. --model-dir Path saved_models No Directory to save the deployable model artifact ( .pkl ). --embedding-cache-dir Path embedding_cache No Directory to cache raw embeddings as .npz files. --output-dir Path results No Directory where evaluation tables and plots are stored. Outputs ¶ Deployable Model Artifact ( <model-dir>/<name>_seed_<seed>_model.pkl ) : Contains the trained PyTorch MLP / Logistic Regression model, StandardScaler, optimal decision threshold, class mapping, and ESM checkpoint metadata. Metrics Summaries ( <output-dir>/ ) : seed_run_summary.csv : Execution summary across seeds. bootstrap_metrics_by_seed.csv : 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, Accuracy, F1, and MCC. seed_predictions.csv : Individual sequence probabilities per seed. Evaluation Plots ( <output-dir>/<name>/seed_<seed>/ ) : Confusion matrix ( .png and .svg ) ROC Curve ( .png and .svg ) Precision-Recall Curve ( .png and .svg ) Example ¶ prime-uncert \ --train results/nonr/Hemolitic-train.fasta \ --test results/nonr/Hemolitic-test.fasta \ --name Hemolitic \ --base-model /data/tiago/prime-validation/checkpoint-500000 \ --seed 200 \ --smote \ --device cuda \ --model-dir results/saved_models \ --embedding-cache-dir results/embedding_cache \ --output-dir results/uncertainty
